locations.quote: **I will build** a platform on which any member of the chair requests time-limited access to any resource, a maintainer decides, and the access ends on its own.

**I follow** the object-oriented software engineering method of Bruegge and Dutoit, and Figure 1 shows the actors and use cases of the platform as a use case diagram in the Unifed Modeling Language. **I pursue** four objectives:

locations.section: 4.1 Structure Resources as an Inheriting Tree
locations.quote: **I will replace** the fat list of hosts and channels with a resource tree whose inner nodes are folders and whose leaves each carry a binding to one target system.

locations.section: 4.1 Structure Resources as an Inheriting Tree
locations.quote: **I will store** the tree with a transitive-closure table of ancestor–descendant pairs and cap the fan-out, so that an approval on the root never reaches the whole infrastructure by accident.

locations.section: 4.2 Design and Implement Connectors with Expiry
locations.quote: **I will defne** one connector contract that validates a binding, grants and revokes access, and optionally lists the current members, and **I will implement** the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors on it.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate Request Review Without Privilege Escalation
locations.quote: **I will build** declarative request forms whose felds, visibility conditions, and rules turn answers into requests for a resource path, a level, and a duration.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate Request Review Without Privilege Escalation
locations.quote: **I will therefore split** the approval: in the review step, the resource owner records a decision without changing Keycloak, and in the grant step, the super admin sets membership and expiry atomically, in bulk for a vetted queue.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate Request Review Without Privilege Escalation
locations.quote: **I will compare** the manual administrative actions and the time to working access with the current process.
**I will attach** a recertifcation interval to each resource, which its descendants inherit, and open a campaign whenever the interval elapses.
The thesis runs from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, and **I divide** it into iterations of two to four weeks.
Outcome: the correctness scenarios pass, and **I measure** the efort.
